featureCatalogue.title: Everything in this alpha
items: A playable regional RPG, rebuilt from the first GitHub prototype into a dimensional pixel-art world.
Explore the feature catalogue and development history below.

sections.title: World and exploration
items: A 2,048 by 1,152 metre overworld with 15 points of interest and seven interiors.
Brookstead, Fern Hollow, Highmere, Alderbridge, the royal relief station, coastal harbor, ruins, clearings and the northern road.
Terraced towns, stone and timber bridges, graded paths, shops, inns, a smithy, civic offices, archives and council rooms.
An interactive 3D atlas of the playable overworld: pan, rotate, zoom, reveal discovery fog, track destinations and fast-travel to discovered locations.
Ground exits and local-map markers; continuous time of day and persistent weather while travelling.

sections.title: Story, companions and quests
items: A playable regional story about the failing Elder Lights, investigations, repairs and the people affected.
Five recruitable companions: Bren, Soren, Tavin, Mira and Lysa, with individual roles, abilities and story-linked Ascensions.
Four Elder Light restorations and six regional story battles lead toward the northern road.
A working opening waterworks quest: free the gate, repair the pump and watch water travel through the depleted river and cascades.
Residents follow village routines; ordinary conversations use speech bubbles, while main-story scenes use portraits.
Optional local requests become available after the opening tutorial.

sections.title: Movement and controls
items: WASD, arrow keys and click-to-move; native eight-direction running and faster Shift sprinting.
A trailing party with shared routes, object clearance and collision against buildings, counters, bridges and railings.
Fixed oblique exploration cameras, individual building and tree cutaways, and side-on battle views.
Mouse, keyboard, arrow-key and Enter support across menus and battle commands.

sections.title: Combat and progression
items: Turn-based battles with visible turn order, party status, enemy status and an overhead target arrow.
Mouse hover and click targeting, double-click attacks and selectable allies for support abilities or items.
Timed three-hit attack chains, skills and magic, MP costs, items, Defend, fleeing and charge-based Ascension.
Melee approaches and recoveries, ranged casting poses, hit reactions and native party and creature animations.
Elemental 3D fire, ice, arcane, lightning, weapon, healing, ward and Ascension effects with dynamic light, smoke, sparks and camera motion.
Combat foliage clearing preserves every fighter’s silhouette; defeated creatures dissolve into colored pixels.
Battle results and growth screens grant experience, gold and rewards once.

sections.title: Inventory, equipment and saves
items: Inventory categories, supplies, equipment, key items, sorting and recipient selection.
Weapon and armor fittings with stat previews, shops, inns, healing, revival and rest services.
Party status, abilities, journal, field guide and local-request pages.
Three journey slots with location, chapter, party, level, playtime and timestamp previews.
Saving and automatic checkpoints are available only inside inns; load, overwrite and delete controls include confirmations and legacy-save support.
Unreadable records can be cleared without deleting other slots or settings.

sections.title: Tutorial and accessibility
items: Guided movement, sprinting, interaction, inventory, party, equipment, abilities, journal, map, saving and settings lessons.
Highlighted interface controls, world arrows, floor encounter markers, replayable narration and lesson skipping.
A scripted first battle teaches target selection, the gold timing window, an MP ability, incoming damage, a practice healing item and Defend.
Adjustable graphics, motion, movement mode, weather and separate music, voice, environment and effects levels.

sections.title: Art, lighting and atmosphere
items: Approved-concept PixelLab characters, monsters, conversation portraits, dedicated HUD portraits and lore illustrations.
Native sprite idle, run, attack, cast and reaction poses; 41 selected character families and 4,878 packed poses.
Varied pixel-art terrain, stone, wood, roofs, props and vegetation with native large surface textures.
Overhead sun and moon lighting, lit sprites, scene shadows, moving cloud shadows and soft sky bounce.
World-space rain, snow, wind, pollen and fireflies; wet surfaces and puddles, water reflections and flowing cascades.
Dense reactive grass and flowers, dimensional foliage, animated waterworks and a diorama focus effect on all four edges.
Live point-of-interest title backgrounds keep residents and scenery animated while hiding the party.

sections.title: Voices, music and sound
items: 385 offline ElevenLabs recordings: 292 dialogue, tutorial and battle performances, plus 93 music, ambience and effects assets.
Five original youthful main voices and supporting casting matched to speakers and portraits.
Thirteen music cues, fourteen environmental loops and sixty-six effects and foley clips.
Spatial footsteps and water, hearth and weather ambience; music transitions and dialogue ducking.
Serialized speech lets narration and story recordings finish without overlapping or replacing one another.

sections.title: Performance and delivery
items: One standalone index.html with the selected artwork, renderer and recordings embedded for offline play.
Instanced vegetation, view-based geometry budgets, pooled combat effects and prepared scene and battle graphics.
Optimized reflection views, bounded river updates, stable frame pacing and cleanup of defeated-enemy shadow resources.
Audited story progression, navigation, saves, native sprite crops, decoded audio and representative performance scenarios.

sections.title: From the first GitHub build to this alpha
items: October 22: the initial Ember and Tide browser game and its source artwork entered GitHub.
October 26: the Elyndor concept rebuild introduced the approved PixelLab cast, portraits, materials, terraced Brookstead and the standalone release.
October 27: connected cascades, world events, combat animation timing, recruitment, interior locations, side-on battles, voices and results screens were developed.
October 28: the full soundscape, inn-only saves, interactive atlas, discovery and fast travel, revised geography, new world materials, guided tutorials and waterworks were integrated.

October 29: the live title and three-slot records, stair and terrain repairs, coherent river water, longer-session optimization, serialized speech, stronger battle visibility, cloud lighting and distinct combat effects form Alpha Version 1.0.

changes: One Alpha Version 1.0 catalogue replaces all incremental changelog entries, with current systems and history from the first GitHub build
Balanced reflections draw one visible pool per frame and high quality draws two; small foliage, precipitation and transient effects are excluded from reflection views
River state remains continuous; geometry is deferred to the next draw, and stable monitor pacing avoids duplicate simulation work after late frames

Overworld vegetation uses padded spatial branches for main, reflection and shadow views; cached static transforms and a single quality budget eliminate redundant matrix work and shadow-target reallocation
Music and environmental stream containers are prepared under the loader with a typed byte loop, removing first-theme-change decoding stalls
Enemy shadow geometry is released at battlefield restoration; scene foliage LOD masks and obsolete renderer lists are disposed with their owners
One recorded speech queue serializes narration, story lines and battle calls; story advances wait for the current spoken line
Projected per-instance color masks keep foreground vegetation off every fighter while preserving shadows and restoring scenery afterwards, including LOD changes
All outdoor locations and the overworld receive a broad, continuously shaded overhead cloud field with coordinated soft moving shadows
Element-specific pooled weapon ribbons, fire coils, ice shards, arcane columns, smoke, sparks, wards and Ascension effects reuse approved textures and dynamic lighting

transcription.scope: Ten new coached-combat narrator performances; all selected words independently transcribed. Original 282 recordings retain their previous verification.

performance.scope: Native Chrome at 1440x900 on the recorded RTX 4080 device. Draw target follows monitor cadence (about 72 Hz here). Tests include repeated travel, filling river, full storm and twenty simultaneous spell effects. Retained heap uses test-only forced GC; runtime does not. Performance varies by hardware.
